name: Operation Anaconda

sides.name: United States and coalition
sides.strength: 10th Mountain Division, 101st Airborne, Special Operations Task Force 11, Afghan militia; about 2,000 in the valley

sides.name: al-Qaeda and Taliban
sides.strength: Estimated 500–1,000 dug into the Shah-i-Kot valley and surrounding ridges

summary: The first large conventional US ground operation of the Afghan war. American infantry helicoptered into the Shah-i-Kot valley in eastern Paktia province to seal al-Qaeda fighters between US blocking positions and Afghan militia. The plan assumed a thin enemy presence; on day one the assault force walked into a heavily fortified network of caves, mortar pits, and ridgelines, and the fight ran for sixteen days.
significance: The Battle of Takur Ghar, where a Navy SEAL fell from a Chinook ramp and the rescue operation cost seven Americans killed, became the defining vignette of the campaign. Operation Anaconda exposed how thin the US-Afghan partnership really was and how deep the enemy had dug in. It set the template for a war that would last twenty years.
